steps.text: In a small bowl, stir together peanut butter, soy sauce, sugar, hot pepper sauce and garlic until well mixed. Gradually stir in water until texture is smooth and creamy.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Peanut Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This spicy peanut sauce can be whipped up in an instant and makes a great addition to many Chinese and Thai recipes.
raw_recipe.name: Best Peanut Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: In a small bowl, stir together peanut butter, soy sauce, sugar, hot pepper sauce and garlic until well mixed. Gradually stir in water until texture is smooth and creamy.

review.reviewBody:
I would have given this recipe 4 stars as is, but it was 5 stars once we tweaked it a bit.

The ratios were a bit off for our tastes. There is too much peanut butter for the amount of other ingredients, so...either add less PB or more of everything else. We just added more of the other ingredients to taste. Extra vinegar and brown sugar (which we used in place of white sugar) was the perfect touch here, as it helps take the place of hoisin sauce. 

My husband used to cook in a high-end restaurant and was skeptical about a hoisin-free peanut sauce, but was very surprised with how good this turned out with our modifications. A few sesame seeds and some green onion on top and it was perfect. (We had it with chicken satay.)
I added a teaspoon of fresh ground pepper, no hot sauce. It was really, really good. I heated it in a small pot and added a little more water to ger the right consistency.

I tweaked it in a variety of ways, thanks to several of the comments, and it was _wonderful_. I used a fresh-ground peanut butter, good soy sauce from an Asian grocery (Gold Mountain?), extra garlic, 1 1/2 t. powdered ginseng, unsweetened coconut milk instead of the water, brown sugar instead of white, 2 T. rice wine, and 3 t. sesame chili oil instead of the hot pepper sauce. 

I also increased the recipe to 6 servings, and served it over lo mein noodles (rinsed in cold water til cool), mixed in with 2 medium carrots (bias-sliced pretty thin), 2 big stalks celery (similarly sliced), and 1/4 of a sweet white onion (sliced _very_ thin from root to end). This made 5-6 general servings. Serve cool ... and it's even better the next day, when the flavors have married.

A big plus for this recipe since it’s incredibly easy, and simple to modify to your own taste. I doubled the soy sauce, sugar and garlic, then added red pepper flakes. If I had read the reviews first, I probably would have added vinegar, burn it turned out great with my modifications (even better than my favorite premade peanut sauce). Sautéed soba noodles with broccoli and tofu, topped with crushed peanuts, green onions and cilantro to make a quick and yummy dinner

Wow! This turned out great. I added vinegar and red pepper flakes instead of the hot sauce, and cooked the sauce so that the sugar (brown instead of white) and vinegar could kind of mix with the seasonings before I threw the peanut butter in. Towards the end I also grated some carrot pieces so that they could wilt but not cook - this turned out great! It was 5 stars at the end, but as it's written it wasn't quite there. Will definitely make again, with my tweaks to the recipe :)

It took a lot of tweaking to get it this where I wanted it. This is a good base to start with, but horrible by itself. I ended up adding fish sauce, garlic powder, ground ginger root, rice vinegar, WAY more sugar, green curry paste, and sesame oil. I can't tell you exact measurements because I just dumped it in there a little at a time. Oh! I almost forgot, if you cook it on low in a sauce pan it makes a HUGE difference in flavor. In the end it turned out full of flavor and just awesome. :)
The recipe is a bit bland, but turned out great with added vinegar, sesame oil and extra hot sauce. Also garnished with sesame seeds and some green onions!
I used brown sugar and added 1 tsp Louisiana hot sauce, 1 tsp tobacco sauce, 1 tsp white vinegar, 1/4 tsp of crushed red pepper, and 1/4 cup crushed peanuts. Just right!

It was good, but I have a lot of plans for this that I think will make it better. I'd like to double everything except for the peanut butter and water, sub honey for the sugar, sub chili garlic sauce for the hot sauce, and add a tablespoon of rice vinegar and a teaspoon of sesame oil.
This recipe is pretty good, but just like TraciA, I tweaked it as well. I went ahead and added the hoisin sauce, because it just wasn't the same without it. I added about a 1/4 cup.

Very nice. Excellent consistency and flavor. I omitted the hot sauce and used fresh garlic. Added 5-6 fresh diced basil leaves. Gourmet without question. Cooked seasoned chicken on top of stove in olive oil, removed it, stirred in sauce, added bite sized chicken and simmered for about 5 min.
The flavor was not quite right and I added extra soy and hot sauce but something was still missing
Ecxellent
I made it as is. I think next time I'll make it spicier for my tastes! It's a great basic sauce you can add your favorite ingredients to make it how you like it!
this recipe as per instructions is absolutely awful. Nothing like the many dozens of restaurants I have ordered it at. I now see why the high rating. Its due to folks changing the recipe. yuck.
My #1 go to for stir fry with chicken or shrimp! I leave out sugar & hot sauce my husband loves it & I'm a peanut butter freak so it works for both of us.

I found this way too salty - maybe add the soy sauce a bit at a time and taste as you go. I adjusted the final product by adding a little extra hot sauce (enough to affect the taste without anyone knowing there's hot sauce in there), some extra vinegar and some sugar. I wouldn't have bothered if I hadn't been trying to disguise the saltiness! With care about the salt, this makes a fine peanut sauce.
Easy to make... always make a double recipe.

I wish I'd read the reviews first...simple sauce but too much peanut butter with a lack of balance of the other ingredients. I tweaked it as I went, but didn't read about the vinegar until afterward. I added vinegar to the remaining sauce and it made a Huge difference. I'll make again but with modifications.

This is a great recipe for starting your own unique sauce.
As many reviews have already mentioned, this recipe requires a little fine tuning which is where YOU get to make it YOUR SAUCE!
First I made the recipe as written and then I made several adjustments to get the flavor and consistency I wanted.
It's been a long time since I've been inspired to try something new, feels good!
